mainTopic: Does ביאה after a failed or conditional קידושין create a marriage? Conditions, mistaken חליצה, and the rulings of רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר, רבי אמי and עולא
overview: This amud asks what happens when a man's קידושין did not work and he then lived with the woman: does the later ביאה make a real marriage? The גמרא first defends רבה's rule that, when only one woman is involved, the man relies on his first קידושין. It shows that the argument in the ברייתא about a minor's קידושין is only about whether people know such קידושין mean nothing. רבי יוחנן is quoted supporting רבה: after conditional קידושין and ביאה, she needs no גט. This is challenged from the rule that a 'mistaken חליצה' is valid. רבי יוחנן defines that as חליצה on condition that she pays 200 זוז, and the challenge argues that doing the act cancels the condition. The answer is that a condition only works on an act a שליח could do, as with בני גד ובני ראובן. קידושין through ביאה is an exception, because all ways of קידושין are linked together. Next, רבי אלעזר, רבי אמי and עולא give different rulings on when ביאה after a failed קידושין requires a גט. The amud ends by quoting רבי ישמעאל, whom עולא rejects: a woman with a mistaken קידושין is never married, even after having a child. His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A case like a one-woman error, and yet they argue
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי אליעזר's view that she does חליצה but not יבום. The גמרא points out that this looks like an error about one woman, yet the תנאים argue, which goes against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי אליעזר they said: she does חליצה but does not do יבום. But here the case is like an error about one woman, and they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא and uses רבי אליעזר's view to challenge רבה, who said no one argues when the error concerns just one woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a man 'married' a girl while she was a minor, which does not count by Torah law, and he lived with her after she grew up. Whether she can do יבום depends on whether that later relationship made a real marriage. That is a one-woman case, and the תנאים argue about it, so it seems that people can argue even in a one-woman case.

keyTerms.meaning: she does חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from her husband's brother
she marries her late husband's brother (יבום)
an error involving just one woman, where the same woman was married with the flawed קידושין
they argue

steps.confusionAlert: The first line is not a new teaching. It is the end of a ברייתא quoted earlier, which the גמרא now uses as ammunition for its challenge.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Eliezer they said:
She performs chalitza but does not enter levirate marriage.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא, דִּכְטָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: But here, it is like an error concerning one woman,
and yet they disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דִּכְטָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת דָּמֵי, וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge against רבה from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that everyone agrees there is no argument in a one-woman case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's case involves one woman, and the תנאים still argue about whether the later relationship made a real marriage.

steps.title: The argument there is about whether people know a minor's marriage means nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's argument is not about dropping a condition. It is about whether an ordinary person knows that a minor's קידושין are worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too they argue about this: one master holds that a person knows a minor's קידושין are nothing, so he decided to live with her for the sake of קידושין. The other master holds that a person does not know a minor's קידושין are nothing, so when he lived with her, he did so based on the first קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by explaining that the ברייתא's argument is about a different question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a man knows the minor's קידושין did nothing, so when he lived with her as an adult he meant to make a new marriage, and יבום is allowed. רבי אליעזר says he does not know this, so he was relying on the worthless first קידושין, and there is no real marriage for יבום. Both sides fit רבה's rule; they only argue about what the man knew.

keyTerms.meaning: the betrothal of a minor girl, which does not count by Torah law in this case
he decided and lived with her (made the relationship count)
for the purpose of making a marriage
based on, with the intention of

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבה's rule stands. When one woman is involved, the man's relationship follows whatever marriage he thinks already exists.

phrases.english: There too, this is what they disagree about:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין קִידּוּשֵׁי קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: One master holds: a person knows that the betrothal of a minor girl is nothing,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who allows יבום.

phrases.english: so he decided and lived with her for the sake of betrothal,
And the other master holds: a person does not know
that the betrothal of a minor girl is nothing,

phrases.english: so when he lives with her, he does so based on the first betrothal.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the argument: it is about what the man knew, not about whether a condition gets dropped.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that תנאים argue even about a one-woman error.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only about whether people know that a minor's קידושין mean nothing; רבה's rule is untouched.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן supports רבה: all agree she needs no גט
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב quotes רבי יוחנן: if a man did קידושין on a condition and then lived with her, everyone agrees she needs no גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רב אחא בר יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: one who did קידושין on a condition and then lived with her, all agree she does not need a גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of an אמורא that agrees with רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says there is no argument at all in this one-woman case. The man's relationship stays tied to the conditional קידושין, so if the condition fails there is no marriage and no גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated; introduces support from another teacher
one who does קידושין on a condition
everyone agrees
a bill of divorce

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Acha bar Yaakov said

One who betrothed a woman on a condition and then lived with her —
[all agree] she does not need a bill of divorce from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה, the גמרא brings positive support for him.

steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement, quoted by רב אחא בר יעקב

steps.title: An objection: a mistaken חליצה is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא, the son of רב איקא and nephew of רב אחא בר יעקב, objects from a ברייתא that says a mistaken חליצה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא, the son of his sister, objected: a mistaken חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: An objection is raised against רבי יוחנן's statement from a ברייתא. The גמרא now needs to explain the ברייתא before we can see how it attacks him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a חליצה done 'by mistake' still works. To see why this challenges רבי יוחנן, the גמרא will first define 'mistaken חליצה' in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection against him from a תנאי source
a mistaken חליצה, done under some wrong understanding
valid

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, the son of his sister, objected to him:
phrases.notes: His sister here means the sister of רב אחא בר יעקב, so the objector is his nephew.

phrases.english: A mistaken chalitza is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the supporting statement of רבי יוחנן brought in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that conditional קידושין followed by living together needs no גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It depends on what 'mistaken חליצה' means, which the גמרא works out in steps 5-8. Step 9 then spells out the attack: if doing the act cancels the condition in חליצה, ביאה should cancel the condition in קידושין too.

steps.title: What is a mistaken חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly 'a mistaken חליצה' means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the objection to define the key term. This sets up the definitions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The force of the objection depends on the definition. A חליצה that is mistaken about its purpose is very different from one done with a condition that later fails.

keyTerms.meaning: which is it, what case is meant

phrases.english: What is a mistaken chalitza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term in the ברייתא from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case that 'mistaken חליצה' refers to

steps.title: ריש לקיש: he was told חליצה would marry her
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a mistaken חליצה is where someone told the brother-in-law: do חליצה with her, and that way you marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: any case where someone tells him, 'Do חליצה with her, and by that you marry her.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives his definition of a mistaken חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the יבם was totally wrong about what חליצה does: he thought it was a way to marry her. Even so, the ברייתא says the חליצה works and releases her.

keyTerms.meaning: do חליצה with her
you bring her in as a wife, you marry her

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Any case where someone says to him,
phrases.notes: Him means the יבם, the brother of the man who died.

phrases.english: 'Perform chalitza with her, and by doing so you marry her.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כֹּל שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A mistaken חליצה is one where the יבם was told that חליצה would marry her.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both must intend the חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's definition. He was taught that a חליצה is invalid unless both the man and the woman intend it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I learn that whether he intended and she did not, or she intended and he did not, her חליצה is invalid until both of them intend it. And you say her חליצה is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back against ריש לקיש's definition, using a teaching he knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חליצה requires the right intention from both people. In ריש לקיש's case the man meant to marry her, not to release her, so the חליצה should be invalid. It cannot be what the ברייתא calls a valid mistaken חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: I learn, I have a ברייתא that teaches
he intended
invalid
both of them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: I teach:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּון הוּא וְלֹא נִתְכַּוְּונָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Whether he intended and she did not intend,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנִּתְכַּוְּונָה הִיא וְלֹא נִתְכַּוֵּון הוּא
phrases.english: or she intended and he did not intend,
her chalitza is invalid,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the definition given in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's definition of a mistaken חליצה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חליצה without the man's intention to release her is invalid, so ריש לקיש's case cannot be called valid.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: חליצה on condition that she pays 200 זוז
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives his own definition: a mistaken חליצה is where the יבם was told to do חליצה on condition that she gives him 200 זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: any case where someone tells him, 'Do חליצה with her on condition that she gives you 200 זוז.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers a new definition of a mistaken חליצה. This sets up the objection against his earlier ruling about conditional קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sides intend a real חליצה, but it is tied to a condition. The ברייתא calls this חליצה valid even though she does not pay, so the condition seems to be dropped by doing the act. That suggests that living with a woman after conditional קידושין might also drop the condition, and the גמרא will develop this objection next.

keyTerms.meaning: on condition that
two hundred זוז, a sum of money

steps.whatToRemember: רבה and רבי יוחנן: after conditional קידושין, living with the same woman keeps the condition, so no גט is needed. The challenge from 'mistaken חליצה' depends on its definition. ריש לקיש's definition is rejected, and רבי יוחנן defines it as חליצה on condition that she pays 200 זוז.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
Any case where someone says to him,
'Perform chalitza with her on condition
that she gives you two hundred zuz.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes she does not end up paying, and the ברייתא still calls the חליצה valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כֹּל שֶׁאוֹמֵר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting ריש לקיש's definition in step 7, רבי יוחנן gives his own.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A mistaken חליצה is one done on condition that she pays 200 זוז.

steps.title: Doing the act means dropping the condition
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא finishes his challenge. In the חליצה case the act counts even though the condition was not met, so the act must cancel the condition. The same should be true for a man who lives with a woman after a conditional קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that once he does the act, he has dropped his condition. Here too, once he has relations with her, he has dropped his condition!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא draws a conclusion from רבי יוחנן's case of the mistaken חליצה. He uses it as a challenge against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's case the יבם did חליצה on condition that he gets 200 זוז, and the ברייתא still says the חליצה is valid. רב אחא reads this as: doing the act shows he gave up the condition. He then applies it to conditional קידושין followed by ביאה, which goes against רב אחא בר יעקב's view that the condition still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / apparently: introduces a conclusion drawn from a source
He fully waived, he gave up (his condition)
A condition
He had relations (with her)
Here too: applying the same logic to the case being discussed

phrases.english: Apparently, since he performed an action,
phrases.notes: The "action" is the חליצה from רבי יוחנן's case, done on condition of getting 200 זוז.

phrases.english: he has waived his condition.
Here too, since he had relations with her,
phrases.notes: "Here" means a man who made קידושין with a condition and then lived with her.

phrases.english: he has waived his condition!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא כֵּיוָן דַּעֲבַד מַעֲשֶׂה אַחוֹלֵי אַחֲלֵיהּ לִתְנָאֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יוחנן's definition from step 8 and turns it into the challenge that was opened in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that a man who lives with a woman after conditional קידושין has not dropped his condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the act of חליצה cancels the condition, then the act of ביאה should cancel the condition too.

steps.title: Conditions only work on acts a שליח could do
steps.stepSummary: The responder (רב אחא בר יעקב, who was being challenged) rejects the proof. We learn all conditions from בני גד ובני ראובן, where the matter was carried out through agents. A condition on an act that cannot be done by a שליח is not a real condition. Since חליצה cannot be done by a שליח, its condition never counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Student of the academy, is that right? After all, where do we learn all the laws of conditions? From the condition of בני גד ובני ראובן. A condition on something that can be done through a שליח, like there, is a real condition. One that cannot be done through a שליח, like there, is not a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The one being challenged answers. The חליצה stood not because the יבם gave up his condition, but because that kind of condition never counted at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of conditions come from משה's deal with בני גד ובני ראובן, and that deal was carried out through agents. So a condition only works on an act that a שליח could do. חליצה must be done by the יבם himself, so the condition was empty from the start. That means the חליצה case proves nothing about waiving a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: Student of the academy: a slightly sharp way of addressing someone
Are you speaking well? Said to push back on an argument
After all: introduces a basic point both sides agree on
The condition משה made with the tribes of גד and ראובן, the source for all laws of conditions
An agent

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule in the laws of conditions: a condition only counts on an act that could be done by a שליח, as in the case of בני גד ובני ראובן.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say he gave up the condition. It says the condition was never valid in the first place, so the question of giving it up does not even come up.

phrases.english: He said to him: Student of the academy,
are you speaking well?
After all, from where do we learn all conditions?
From the condition of the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuven.
A condition on something that can be carried out
phrases.notes: He means the act the condition is attached to. For example, nobody else can do חליצה for you.

phrases.english: through an agent, like there,
phrases.notes: "There" means בני גד ובני ראובן, where משה handed the job over to others to carry out.

phrases.english: its condition is a real condition.
One that cannot be carried out
through an agent, like there,
is not a condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר בֵּי רַב שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's challenge by giving a different reason why the חליצה stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the source: the condition was never valid, rather than being waived.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חליצה stood because doing the act showed he gave up his condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חליצה stood because a condition on an act that a שליח cannot do is not a condition at all, so nothing can be learned about ביאה from it.

steps.title: But a condition on ביאה does count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule. קידושין through ביאה cannot be done by a שליח, and yet a condition attached to it is a valid condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ביאה cannot be done through a שליח like there, and yet a condition on it counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 10 using a known case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said a condition only works on acts a שליח could do. But it is accepted that a man who does קידושין through ביאה with a condition has made a valid condition, even though no שליח can do ביאה for him. So the rule seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But look: opens a challenge
Relations, here as a way of doing קידושין
And yet it is

phrases.english: But relations,
phrases.notes: He means קידושין done through relations, with a condition attached.

phrases.english: which cannot be carried out
through an agent like there,
and yet it is a valid condition!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בִּיאָה דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לְקַיּוֹמַיהּ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just set out in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a condition on an act that cannot be done through a שליח is not a condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קידושין through ביאה cannot be done through a שליח, yet a condition on it is accepted as valid, so the rule seems wrong.

steps.title: Conditions on ביאה work because all ways of קידושין are linked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that קידושין through ביאה can carry a condition only because the Torah links all forms of קידושין together.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in קידושין, it is different, because all the ways of 'becoming' married are compared to one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. It explains why a condition works on קידושין through ביאה even though ביאה cannot be done by a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses one word, 'becoming' a wife, for all three ways of קידושין: money, a document, and ביאה. Money and a document can be done through a שליח, so conditions on them work. Because ביאה is linked to them, a condition on ביאה works too. So the rule from step 10 still stands: חליצה has no such link, so its condition still does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The ways of 'becoming' a wife: money, a document, and ביאה
They are compared or linked together by the Torah
To each other

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the rule from step 10. Only an act that can be done by a שליח can carry a condition, and קידושין through ביאה is a special exception because of the link.

phrases.english: There, by קידושין,
it is because the ways of 'becoming' married are compared to each other.
phrases.notes: 'Becoming' comes from the words 'and she becomes another man's wife' (דברים 24:2). It covers all three ways of קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by showing that קידושין through ביאה is a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special source (היקש) that makes this case different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ביאה cannot be done by a שליח, a condition on it should not count, which would break the rule from step 10.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. ביאה can carry a condition only because the Torah links it to money and a document, which can be done by a שליח.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: in all three failed cases followed by ביאה, she needs a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that if the first קידושין failed (a loan, an unmet condition, or less than a פרוטה) and the man then lived with her, everyone agrees she needs a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עולא בר אבא said in the name of עולא, who said in the name of רבי אלעזר: If someone does קידושין with a loan and then lives with her, or on a condition and then lives with her, or with less than a פרוטה and then lives with her, everyone agrees she needs a גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a man whose first קידושין did not work and who later lived with the woman. רבי אלעזר says that in all three cases she needs a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the first קידושין did not take effect. A loan does not count as money for קידושין. The condition was not met. Less than a פרוטה is not enough value. Still, רבי אלעזר says the later ביאה counts as a new קידושין, so she is married and needs a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan. Here the man tries to do קידושין by cancelling a debt she owes him.
He lived with her as husband and wife
The value of a פרוטה, the smallest amount that works for קידושין
Everyone agrees
A bill of divorce

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר does not say the first קידושין worked. It did not work. She needs a גט because of the ביאה that came afterward.

phrases.english: Rav Ulla bar Abba said
that Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
One who does קידושין with a loan and then lives with her,
or on a condition and then lives with her,
phrases.notes: The case is where the condition was not met.

phrases.english: or with less than a פרוטה's worth and then lives with her —
everyone agrees she needs a גט from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עוּלָּא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opposing tradition to רבי יוחנן's statement in step 3. Where רבי יוחנן said all agree no גט is needed after conditional קידושין and ביאה, רבי אלעזר says all agree a גט is needed, and he adds the loan and less-than-a-פרוטה cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After any of these three failed קידושין, a later ביאה makes her married, so she needs a גט.

steps.title: רבי אמי: only less than a פרוטה needs a גט, because the man may err in the others
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says a גט is needed only when the קידושין was with less than a פרוטה. In the loan and condition cases the man may have made a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר אבא said in the name of רבי מנחם, who said in the name of רבי אמי: If someone does קידושין with less than a פרוטה and then lives with her, she needs a גט from him. In this case he does not make a mistake, but in those other cases he does make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion limits רבי אלעזר's ruling. Only the less-than-a-פרוטה case needs a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that קידושין needs at least a פרוטה. So the man knew his first קידושין failed, and he must have meant the ביאה as a new קידושין. With a loan or a condition, he may have wrongly thought the first קידושין worked, so he did not mean the ביאה to be a new קידושין, and no גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes a mistake
In those other cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows what the whole question depends on: what the man was thinking when he lived with her. If he knew the first קידושין failed, the ביאה counts as קידושין.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Abba said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מְנַחֵם אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Menachem said that Rabbi Ami said:
One who does קידושין with less than a פרוטה's worth and then lives with her,
she needs a גט from him.
It is in this case that he does not make a mistake,
phrases.notes: Everyone knows a פרוטה is the smallest amount, so he knew the first קידושין failed.

phrases.english: but in those other cases he does make a mistake.
phrases.notes: He means the loan case and the condition case from רבי אלעזר's list.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי מְנַחֵם אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר and narrows his ruling to only one of the three cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only after קידושין with less than a פרוטה does a later ביאה require a גט. In the loan and condition cases the man may have made a mistake, so no גט is needed.

steps.title: עולא: a conditional קידושין followed by ביאה needs a גט, as in a real case
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא quotes עולא that after a conditional קידושין and ביאה she needs a גט. He tells of a real case where the חכמים could not free the woman without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of עולא: If someone does קידושין on a condition and then lives with her, she needs a גט from him. This really happened, and the חכמים did not have the power to send her away without a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A third statement agrees with רבי אלעזר about the condition case. It backs this up with a story that really happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against רבי אמי, עולא holds that even in the condition case the later ביאה makes her married, so she needs a גט. The real case shows the ruling was used in practice: the חכמים could not treat her as unmarried, so she could leave only with a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
A real case that happened
To release her or send her away from the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on ביאה after a failed קידושין: רבי אלעזר says a גט is needed in all three cases. רבי אמי says only in the less-than-a-פרוטה case. עולא, through רב כהנא, says a גט is needed in the condition case, and a real case was decided that way.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said in the name of Ulla:
One who does קידושין on a condition and then lives with her —
she needs a גט from him.
This was a real case,
and the חכמים did not have the power
to release her without a גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's ruling in the condition case, against רבי אמי, and adds a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a conditional קידושין followed by ביאה, she needs a גט. A real case was decided this way.

steps.title: עולא's ruling rejects a certain תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says עולא's ruling is meant to reject the view of a specific תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling comes to exclude the view of this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that עולא's ruling disagrees with an earlier תנא, and it is about to quote that תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said that after a conditional קידושין followed by ביאה, the woman needs a גט. The גמרא now points out that this goes against a תנא who thinks a mistaken קידושין can be ignored completely, with no גט at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject another view
A sage from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: To exclude the view of this Tanna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which earlier opinion עולא's ruling (step 15) is arguing against.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולא's ruling disagrees with a תנא who holds that a mistaken קידושין needs no גט.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a woman who was forced is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק of סוטה that a woman who was not forced is forbidden to her husband, so a woman who was forced is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, quoting רבי ישמעאל: The פסוק says "and she was not seized," so she is forbidden. This means that if she was seized, she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the תנא it just mentioned. רבי ישמעאל first reads the פסוק about a סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a wife who was unfaithful "and she was not seized," meaning she acted willingly. Only then is she forbidden to her husband. So if she was forced, she stays permitted to him. This is the base rule that his next point builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: She was seized, meaning forced
Forbidden to her husband
Permitted to her husband
A wife suspected of being unfaithful

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
In the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
"And she was not seized": she is forbidden.
This implies that if she was seized, she is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the תנא that step 16 said עולא disagrees with.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who was forced is permitted to her husband. Only a willing wife is forbidden.

steps.title: Another permitted woman: a mistaken קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל adds that a woman whose קידושין was a mistake is permitted even if she acted willingly. This applies even after she has had a child from this marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is another woman who is permitted even though she was not forced. Who is she? A woman whose קידושין was a mistaken קידושין, so that even if her son is riding on her shoulders…
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל adds a second case where a woman stays permitted even though she acted willingly: when her קידושין was mistaken. The sentence keeps going in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her קידושין was a mistake, so she was never truly married. Her willing act is therefore not adultery at all. Even after years together and a child, the marriage counts as nothing. That is exactly why this view clashes with עולא, who says a גט is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken קידושין, which does not take effect
Another case
Riding on her shoulders

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think she is permitted because she was forced. She acted willingly. She is permitted only because her mistaken קידושין never made her a married woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opinion that עולא rejects. רבי ישמעאל treats a mistaken קידושין as nothing at all, even after they lived together and had a child.

phrases.english: And you have another woman

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה, מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: Who, even though she was not seized, is permitted.
And who is this?
One whose betrothal was a mistaken betrothal,
So that even if her son is riding on her shoulders,
phrases.notes: He means a son from this marriage. The sentence isn't finished yet; it continues in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ לְךָ אַחֶרֶת שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְפָּשָׂה מוּתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule in step 17 by adding a second woman who is permitted even though she was not forced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with a mistaken קידושין is not a married woman. Her willing act does not forbid her, even after she has had a child.
